description: Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is a beloved Italian flatbread, originating from the Liguria region, known for its irresistibly soft, airy texture and golden, crisp crust. Drizzled generously with extra virgin olive oil and fragrant rosemary, it boasts a simple yet profound flavor that makes it a perfect accompaniment to any meal or a delightful snack on its own. This classic recipe brings the authentic taste of Genoa directly to your kitchen, inviting you to savor a true piece of Italian culinary heritage.

ingredients.notes: plus more for drizzling and pan

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active. This step is crucial for a light and airy focaccia.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: Add the all-purpose flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Pour in 30ml of the extra virgin olive oil. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface.

instructions.title: Knead the Dough
instructions.text: Knead the dough for about 10-15 minutes until it becomes smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. You can use a stand mixer with a dough hook for 8-10 minutes on medium-low speed. Form the dough into a ball.

instructions.title: First Rise
instructions.text: Lightly oil a clean bowl with a little olive oil. Place the dough ball in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap or a damp kitchen towel. Let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until it has doubled in size.

instructions.title: Shape and Second Rise
instructions.text: Generously grease a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking pan with 30ml of extra virgin olive oil. Gently transfer the risen dough to the pan. Using your fingertips, gently stretch the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to deflate it too much. Drizzle with another 20ml of olive oil. Cover the pan with plastic wrap and let it rise again for 20-30 minutes.

instructions.title: Dimple and Top
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 220C (425F). Uncover the focaccia. Using your oiled fingertips, gently press dimples all over the surface of the dough, creating small indentations. Drizzle with a final touch of olive oil, sprinkle with fresh rosemary, and flaky sea salt.

instructions.title: Bake to Golden Perfection
instructions.text: Bake the focaccia in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until it is golden brown on top and cooked through. The crust should be crisp and the interior soft. Once baked, carefully remove it from the oven.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Transfer the focaccia to a wire rack to cool slightly before slicing. Serve warm or at room temperature. It is delicious on its own, with a meal, or dipped in more extra virgin olive oil.

tips: For the characteristic airy texture, ensure your dough is well-hydrated and knead it thoroughly until smooth and elastic. The long, slow fermentation is key.
Always use high-quality extra virgin olive oil, especially for the final drizzle and topping, as its flavor is paramount to authentic Focaccia Genovese.
Focaccia is best enjoyed fresh on the day it is baked. If you have leftovers, store them in an airtight container at room temperature and reheat briefly in the oven for best results.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the sun-drenched Ligurian coast of Italy, where simple ingredients are transformed into a masterpiece of texture and flavor: Focaccia Genovese. This iconic flatbread, a staple of Italian baking, is more than just bread; it's a testament to the power of high-quality olive oil, fragrant rosemary, and a touch of salt. Often enjoyed throughout the day, from breakfast to an evening aperitivo, its irresistible aroma and tender crumb have captivated palates worldwide. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that authentic Italian bakery experience in your own kitchen, this comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know about crafting the perfect Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil. Prepare to impress your senses and your guests with this delightful, aromatic bread.

## What is Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil?
At its heart, Focaccia Genovese is a traditional Ligurian flatbread characterized by its unique preparation and incredible texture. Unlike other focaccia styles, the Genovese version is known for being exceptionally soft, airy, and drenched in olive oil – both incorporated into the dough and generously drizzled on top before baking. The hallmark of a true Focaccia Genovese is its dimpled surface, created by pressing fingers into the dough, which allows pools of olive oil and brine to collect, resulting in pockets of savory deliciousness. The addition of fresh rosemary and a sprinkle of coarse sea salt further elevates its simple yet profound flavor profile, making Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil a truly unforgettable treat. Its history stretches back centuries, with local bakers perfecting the art of a perfectly crisp exterior giving way to a cloud-like interior, a balance achieved through precise hydration and careful handling.

## Ingredients You Need
Crafting authentic Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil requires a handful of quality ingredients. Don't skimp on the olive oil; it's the star of the show!

*   **All-Purpose Flour (or "00" Flour):** Approximately 500 grams (about 4 cups). "00" flour, if available, provides a finer crumb, but good quality all-purpose works beautifully.
*   **Warm Water:** About 350-400 ml (1.5 to 1.75 cups). The exact amount can vary based on your flour and environment, so add gradually. It should be lukewarm, around 105-115°F (40-46°C), to activate the yeast.
*   **Active Dry Yeast:** 7 grams (about 2.25 teaspoons or one standard packet).
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** 10 grams (about 1.5 teaspoons) for the dough, plus extra for sprinkling on top.
*   **Sugar (optional):** 5 grams (about 1 teaspoon). A touch of sugar helps activate the yeast and can contribute to browning.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** At least 100 ml (about 1/2 cup) for the dough, plus another 50-75 ml (1/4 to 1/3 cup) for drizzling, and more for greasing the pan. Use a good quality, fruity extra virgin olive oil – it makes a huge difference.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** 2-3 sprigs, leaves stripped and roughly chopped.
*   **Coarse Sea Salt (e.g., Maldon):** For finishing.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the warm water, yeast, and sugar (if using). Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy. This indicates the yeast is active.
2.  **Combine Dry Ingredients:** In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour and fine sea salt.
3.  **Form the Dough:** Pour the activated yeast mixture into the flour mixture. Add 50 ml (1/4 cup) of extra virgin olive oil. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms.
4.  **Knead the Dough:** Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for 8-10 minutes until it's smooth and elastic. If using a stand mixer, use the dough hook for 6-8 minutes on medium-low speed. The dough will be quite soft and sticky – resist adding too much extra flour.
5.  **First Proof:** Lightly oil a large bowl. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
6.  **Prepare the Pan:** Generously grease a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking pan with extra virgin olive oil. Be liberal; this contributes to the crispy bottom.
7.  **Transfer and Dimple:** Gently transfer the risen dough to the prepared pan. Pour another 25 ml (about 1.5 tablespoons) of olive oil over the dough. Using your fingertips, gently press and stretch the dough to fill the pan, creating characteristic dimples across the entire surface. Don't deflate it completely.
8.  **Second Proof:** Sprinkle the chopped fresh rosemary evenly over the dough. Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap or a damp towel and let it proof again for 30-45 minutes, or until noticeably puffy.
9.  **Preheat Oven:** While the dough is proofing for the second time, preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C).
10. **Final Touches and Bake:** Once the dough is puffy, drizzle another 25-50 ml (1/4 cup or more) of extra virgin olive oil generously over the surface, ensuring the dimples are filled. Sprinkle liberally with coarse sea salt.
11. **Bake:** Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is golden brown on top and cooked through. The bottom should also be nicely browned and crispy.
12. **Cool:** Remove from the oven and, if desired, drizzle with a final touch of olive oil. Let it cool in the pan for a few minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

*   **Quality Olive Oil is Non-Negotiable:** This cannot be stressed enough. A good extra virgin olive oil contributes immensely to the flavor, aroma, and texture of your Focaccia Genovese. It’s worth investing in a high-quality bottle.
*   **Hydration is Key:** Focaccia dough is a high-hydration dough, meaning it's quite wet and sticky. Resist the urge to add too much flour during kneading or shaping. This high hydration is what gives it its characteristic airy, open crumb.
*   **Patience with Proofing:** Don't rush the proofing stages. Proper rising develops flavor and creates that beautiful, airy texture. A warm, draft-free environment is ideal.
*   **Generous Dimpling:** The dimples are not just for aesthetics; they create pockets for the olive oil and brine to collect, ensuring maximum flavor and moisture in every bite. Don't be shy!
*   **The Brine Trick (Optional but Recommended):** For an even more authentic Genovese flavor, some bakers create a simple brine (1 part water, 1 part olive oil, a pinch of salt) to pour into the dimples just before baking. This helps create those irresistible savory pockets.
*   **Don't Overbake:** Keep an eye on your focaccia. While you want a golden crust, overbaking can dry it out.
*   **Warm Serving:** While delicious at room temperature, Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is truly magical when served slightly warm, allowing its aromas to fully bloom.

## Serving Suggestions
Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in countless ways:

*   **As is:** Its rich flavor makes it perfect for eating on its own, perhaps with a cup of coffee for breakfast or a glass of wine for an aperitivo.
*   **With Dips:** Serve it alongside a good balsamic glaze, pesto, or a simple olive oil dip with herbs.
*   **Accompaniment to Meals:** It's an excellent bread to serve with soups, stews, salads, or pasta dishes, perfect for soaking up delicious sauces.
*   **Sandwiches:** Slice it horizontally and fill it with your favorite Italian deli meats, cheeses, roasted vegetables, or a fresh caprese salad for an elevated sandwich experience.
*   **Cheese Board:** A beautiful addition to any cheese board, complementing both soft and hard cheeses.

## Variations and Substitutions
While the classic Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is perfect as is, you can certainly experiment with other flavors:

*   **Olives:** Press pitted black or green olives into the dough before the second proof.
*   **Cherry Tomatoes:** Halved cherry tomatoes can be nestled into the dimples for a burst of sweetness and acidity.
*   **Onions:** Thinly sliced red onions, caramelized or raw, add a pungent sweetness.
*   **Garlic:** minced fresh garlic can be added to the olive oil drizzle before baking.
*   **Other Herbs:** While rosemary is traditional, you can substitute or add other fresh herbs like thyme, oregano, or sage.
*   **Cheese:** A sprinkle of grated Parmesan or Pecorino Romano during the last few minutes of baking can add a savory, cheesy crust.
*   **Spices:** A pinch of red pepper flakes can introduce a subtle heat.
*   **Gluten-Free:** While challenging to replicate the exact texture, gluten-free flour blends specifically designed for yeast breads can be used, though adjustments to water content and proofing times may be necessary.

Baking your own Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is a rewarding experience that fills your home with an intoxicating aroma and your table with a piece of Italian culinary heritage. With a little patience and good quality ingredients, you’ll be enjoying this delightful flatbread in no time. Buon appetito!
